# Setup

Install packages:
```{r}
install.packages("svglite")
```

Load packages:

```{r setup}
package_list <- c(
  'tidyverse', 'terra', 'sf', 'landscapemetrics', "parallel", "DT", "corrplot",
  "FactoMineR", "factoextra", "broom", "ggrepel", "svglite"
  )

invisible(
  lapply(
    package_list,
    require,
    character.only = TRUE
  )
)
```

Source functions.

```{r}
invisible(
  lapply(
    list.files('functions/', full.names = TRUE),
    source)
  )
```


# Loading Input Data

Get input file locations.

```{r}
# location of sample coordinate file
#sample_coordinate_location <- "input_data/00_sample_data/samples_coords.csv"

# location of sample files
sample_file_location <-
  "/mnt/data2/Project_Polli_agro/Operational/4_data_analysis/7_seldetection/environmental_data/input_data/00_sample_data/ALL_samples_metadata_complete.csv"
```

## Sample Metadata input

Load and tidy sample coordinate data. This table contains data for all samples, even those not used in the SSF analysis.

```{r}
sample_metadata <- read.csv(sample_file_location)
```

Create a separate dataframe with only poll data.

```{r}
final_poll_metadata <- sample_metadata %>%
  select(poll, location, landscape_level_1, landscape_level_2, LAT, LONG) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(poll)

final_poll_metadata %>% datatable()
```

# Land Use Analysis

## Extract Landscape Metrics

### Read and Tidy Land Use Data

Load land use data for Portugal. 
The merged raster was created from Sentinel rasters '29S' and '29T' with `gdal` in `merge_sentinel_rasters.sh`.

```{r}
sentinel_landuse_raster = rast(
  'input_data/01_raster_data/00_sentinel_land_use_rasters/sentinel_29S_29T_joined.tif', 
  )
```

Add names to land use classes.

```{r}
# create dataframe with id - class key
land_use_classes <- data.frame(
  id = c(1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11),
  landuse = c(
    "Water", "Trees", "Flooded vegetation", "Crops", "Built Area",
    "Bare ground", "Snow/Ice", "Clouds", "Rangeland"
    )
  )

# add info to raster
levels(sentinel_landuse_raster) <- land_use_classes
```

Plot raster.

```{r}
plot(sentinel_landuse_raster)
```

### Create Rasters for Each Sampling Landscape

Create a 1 km buffer around each geographical coordinate.

```{r}
# convert coordinates for each poll into a SpatVector object
poll_coords_sv = vect(
  final_poll_metadata, 
  geom = c('LONG' ,'LAT'),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
  )

# check if names were stored
poll_coords_sv$poll

# coordinate reference system must match that of the land use raster
# it is easier to re-project vector than re-project the raster
poll_coords_sv = project(x = poll_coords_sv, crs(sentinel_landuse_raster))

# create 1 km buffers around each point
poll_buffers_sv = buffer(poll_coords_sv, width = 1000)
```

Use buffer area to crop the land use raster, creating 78.54 km² landscape for each poll.

```{r}
# create a raster for each poll and store them in a list
poll_landuse_raster_list <- lapply(
  1:nrow(poll_buffers_sv),
  \(x) crop_raster_with_buffer(poll_buffers_sv[x, 1], sentinel_landuse_raster)
  )

# set list entry names
names(poll_landuse_raster_list) <- poll_buffers_sv$poll


```


```{r}
for (poll in names(poll_landuse_raster_list)) {
  
  jpeg(filename = paste0("results/poll_landscape_buffers/", poll, ".jpg"))
  poll_landuse_raster_list[[poll]] %>% 
    plot(
      main = poll,
      plg = list(title="Land Use Class"))
  dev.off()
  
}
```


### Extract Landscape Metrics for Each Sampling Landscape

Check the input landscapes.

```{r}
check_landscape(poll_landuse_raster_list) %>% datatable()
```

Create list of `landscapemetrics` functions to use on our landscapes.

```{r}
landscapemetrics_function_list <- c(
  lsm_l_area_cv, lsm_l_area_mn, lsm_l_area_sd, lsm_l_cohesion, lsm_l_condent,
  lsm_l_contag, lsm_l_contig_cv, lsm_l_contig_mn, lsm_l_contig_sd, lsm_l_ed,
  lsm_l_ent, lsm_l_iji, lsm_l_joinent,
  lsm_l_lpi, lsm_l_np, lsm_l_pd, lsm_l_pr, lsm_l_prd, lsm_l_shdi, lsm_l_shei, 
  lsm_l_sidi, lsm_l_siei, lsm_l_ta, lsm_l_te, lsm_c_ca
  )

# lsm_l_enn_cv, lsm_l_enn_mn, lsm_l_enn_sd,
```

Calculate metrics for each landscape.

```{r}
# apply calculate_landscape_metrics() to each raster
poll_landscapemetrics_df <- parallel::mclapply(
  poll_landuse_raster_list,
  \(x) calculate_landscape_metrics(x, landscapemetrics_function_list),
  mc.cores = 79
  ) %>%
  # bind list entries into a dataframe
  bind_rows()

write.csv(poll_landscapemetrics_df, "results/landscape_metrics/raw_landscape_metrics.csv")
```

```{r}
poll_landscapemetrics_df %>% datatable()
```

# Landuse Class Composition Analysis

## Transform Data

Calculate the proportion of area occupied by each landscape type in each sampling location.

Because some landscapes include a lot of area covered by water, especially those close to the coast, it is necessary to calculate the proportions subtracting the area covered by water from the total area.

```{r calculate_landscape_metrics}
# calculate the area occupied by each class in each sampling location
poll_landuse_class_area <- poll_landscapemetrics_df %>%
  filter(
    metric %in% c("ca", "ta")
    ) %>%
  left_join(
    final_poll_metadata
    ) %>%
  left_join(
    land_use_classes, by = join_by(class == id)
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = case_when(
      metric == "ca" ~ paste0(metric, "_", landuse),
      .default = metric
      )
    ) %>%
  # sum polls belonging to each sampling location
  summarise(
    total_area = sum(value),
    .by = c(location, metric) # important
    ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = metric,
    values_from = total_area,
    values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
  # join location metadata
  left_join(
    final_poll_metadata %>%
      select(location, landscape_level_1, landscape_level_2) %>%
      distinct(),
    "location"
    ) 

# transform class areas into class proportions in relation to total landscape area
poll_landuse_class_prop <- poll_landuse_class_area %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      starts_with("ca_"),
      \(x) x/ta
      )
    ) 

# transform class areas into class proportions in relation to total landscape 
# area that is not water
poll_landuse_class_prop_nw <- poll_landuse_class_area %>%
  mutate(
    ta_minus_water = ta - ca_Water,
    across(
      starts_with("ca_"),
      \(x) x/ta_minus_water
      )
    ) %>%
  select(-ta, -ca_Water)

# write files
write_csv(poll_landuse_class_area, "results/landscape_metrics/poll_landuse_class_area.csv")
write_csv(poll_landuse_class_prop, "results/landscape_metrics/poll_landuse_class_propotion.csv")
write_csv(poll_landuse_class_prop_nw, "results/landscape_metrics/poll_landuse_class_propotion_no_water.csv")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
datatable(poll_landuse_class_prop_nw)
```

```{r}

#| fig-height: 6
poll_landuse_class_prop_nw %>%
  pivot_longer(
    starts_with("ca_"),
    names_to = "class",
    values_to = "proportion"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    class = str_remove(class, "ca_")
  ) %>%
  # filter(
  #   proportion > 0#,
```

## Statistical Tests

Transform data into long format.

```{r}
poll_landuse_class_prop_long <- 
  poll_landuse_class_prop_nw %>%
  select(
    Location = location,
    landscape_level_1,
    landscape_level_2,
    starts_with("ca")
    ) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("ca_"), names_to = "Class", values_to = "Proportion") %>% 
  mutate(Class = str_remove(Class, "ca_"))
```

Compare SSF and LoA.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10
p3<- poll_landuse_class_prop_long %>% 
  ggstatsplot::grouped_ggbetweenstats(
    x = landscape_level_1,
    y = Proportion,
    grouping.var = Class, 
    type = "nonparametric",
    pairwise.display = "significant", ## display only significant pairwise comparisons
    p.adjust.method = "fdr", ## adjust p-values for multiple tests using this method
    centrality.plotting = FALSE,
    ggtheme = theme_bw(),
    ggplot.component = list(
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"), 
        axis.title.x.bottom = element_blank(),
        aspect.ratio = .5
        )
      ),
    package = "ggsci",
    palette = "default_jco",
    ggsignif.args = list(textsize = 2.5, tip_length = 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    plotgrid.args = list(ncol = 2, widths = 1)
    )

ggsave(
  filename = "Statistical_comparison_SSF_LoA.svg",
  plot = p3,
  device = svglite::svglite,
  width = 10,
  height = 10
)
```

Compare SSF and LoA Near/Far.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10
p4<- poll_landuse_class_prop_long %>% 
  ggstatsplot::grouped_ggbetweenstats(
    x = landscape_level_2,
    y = Proportion,
    grouping.var = Class, 
    type = "nonparametric",
    pairwise.display = "significant", ## display only significant pairwise comparisons
    p.adjust.method = "fdr", ## adjust p-values for multiple tests using this method
    centrality.plotting = FALSE,
    ggtheme = theme_bw(),
    ggplot.component = list(
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"), 
        axis.title.x.bottom = element_blank(),
        aspect.ratio = .5
        )
      ),
    ggsignif.args = list(textsize = 2, tip_length = 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    plotgrid.args = list(ncol = 2, widths = 1)
    )

ggsave(
  filename = "Statistical_comparison_SSF_Near_LoA_Near_Far.svg",
  plot = p4,
  device = svglite::svglite,
  width = 10,
  height = 10
)
```

## Correlation Between Land Use Classes

```{r}
# calculate Pearson correlation
poll_landuse_class_correlation <- cor(
  poll_landuse_class_prop_nw %>%
    select(-ta_minus_water, -landscape_level_1, -landscape_level_2) %>%
    column_to_rownames("location")
  )
```

Plot correlation matrix.

```{r}
svglite::svglite("poll_landuse_correlation.svg", width = 8, height = 8)

corrplot(
  poll_landuse_class_correlation,
  method = "number",
  order = "hclust",
  addrect = 2
)

dev.off()
```

**This shows that:**

- Proportion of Rangeland is negatively correlated to the proportion of Crops, Trees, and Built Area;
- Proportion of Trees is negatively correlated to the proportion of Crops.

## Principal Components Analysis

Run PCA.

```{r}
poll_landuse_class_pca <- PCA(
  poll_landuse_class_prop_nw %>%
    select(-ta_minus_water) %>%
    column_to_rownames("location"),
  scale.unit = TRUE,
  quali.sup = 6:7,
  graph = FALSE
  )
```

Check variance.

```{r}
poll_landuse_class_pca$eig %>% datatable()

fviz_screeplot(poll_landuse_class_pca, ncp=10)
```

**The first 3 dimensions together explain almost 90% of variation**.

Check variable contribution to each of the three dimentions.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

poll_landuse_class_pca$var$cos2 %>% datatable()
poll_landuse_class_pca$var$cos2 %>% heatmap()

fviz_pca_var(axes = c(1,2),
  poll_landuse_class_pca,
  col.var = "cos2",
  gradient.cols = c("black", "orange", "green"),
  repel = TRUE
  )

fviz_pca_var(axes = c(1,3),
  poll_landuse_class_pca,
  col.var = "cos2",
  gradient.cols = c("black", "orange", "green"),
  repel = TRUE
  )

fviz_pca_var(axes = c(2,3),
  poll_landuse_class_pca,
  col.var = "cos2",
  gradient.cols = c("black", "orange", "green"),
  repel = TRUE
  )
```

Dim1:
- Most influenced by **proportion of crops, rangeland and built area**; 

Dim2:
- Most influenced by **proportion of trees and rangeland**;

Dim3: 
- Most influenced by **proportion of bare ground**;

Check samples.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

fviz_pca_biplot(
  axes = c(1,2),
  poll_landuse_class_pca,
  label = "all",
  col.var = "black",
  habillage = 6
  )

fviz_pca_biplot(
  axes = c(1,2),
  poll_landuse_class_pca,
  label = "all",
  col.var = "black",
  habillage = 7
  )

ggsave(filename = "results/landscape_metrics/PCA_SSF_LoA_class_composition.pdf", width = 10, height = 8)
```

Dim1 separates SSF (more built area and crops) from LoA (more rangeland).
Dim2 separates landscapes based on proportion of rangeland and trees.
Dim3 separates landscapes based on proportion of bare ground.

### Publication Plot

PCA.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8

variance <- poll_landuse_class_pca$eig[,2]

ind_coords <-
  get_pca_ind(poll_landuse_class_pca)$coord %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Location") %>% 
  left_join(
    final_poll_metadata %>%
      select(Location = location, landscape_level_1, landscape_level_2) %>%
      distinct()
    ) %>% 
  mutate(Location = str_replace_all(Location, "_", " "))

var_coords <-
  get_pca_var(poll_landuse_class_pca)$coord %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Variable") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = str_remove(Variable, "ca_"))

pca_plot <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), color = "lightgrey") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 0), color = "lightgrey") +
  geom_point(
    data = ind_coords, 
    aes(x = Dim.1, y = Dim.2, fill = landscape_level_2),
    shape = 21, color = "black", size = 2
    ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = var_coords,
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = (`Dim.1`*2), yend = (`Dim.2`*2)),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(1/2, "picas")),
    color = "black"
    ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = ind_coords,
    aes(x = (`Dim.1`), y = (`Dim.2`), label = Location),
    size = 4
    ) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = var_coords,
    aes(x = (`Dim.1`*2), y = (`Dim.2`*2), label = Variable),
    size = 4, force = 3
    ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title="Landscape Category", )) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(variance[1],1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(variance[2],1), "%)")
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(.99,.99),
    legend.justification = c(1, 1),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black", linewidth = .2)
    )

pca_plot

ggview::save_ggplot(pca_plot, width = 8, height = 8, "results/landscape_metrics/PCA_SSF_LoA_class_composition.svg")
```

# Landscape Metrics Analysis

## Transform Data 

Poll026 (Arruda) and poll052 (São Mamede) have less than 3 landuse classes and several metrics cannot be calculated, returning NAs. Because of this, NAs are ignored when calculating the median values for each sampling location.

```{r}
# calculate the median and mean of each metric in each location
poll_landuse_metrics_summary <- poll_landscapemetrics_df %>%
  filter(
    !metric %in% c("ca", "ta")
    ) %>%
  left_join(
    final_poll_metadata
    ) %>%
  left_join(
    land_use_classes, by = join_by(class == id)
    ) %>%
  # calculate median, mean, and standard deviation
  summarise(
    median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm= TRUE),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(location, metric)
    )

poll_landuse_metrics_median <- poll_landuse_metrics_summary %>%
  select(location, metric, median) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = metric,
    values_from = median,
    values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
  # join location metadata
  left_join(
    final_poll_metadata %>%
      select(location, landscape_level_1, landscape_level_2) %>%
      distinct(),
    "location"
    ) 

write_csv(poll_landuse_metrics_summary, "results/landscape_metrics/poll_landuse_metrics_mean_median_sd.csv")
write.csv(poll_landuse_metrics_median, "results/landscape_metrics/poll_landuse_metrics_median.csv")
```

## Correlation Between LandscapeMetrics

```{r}
# calculate Pearson correlation
poll_landuse_metrics_correlation <- cor(
  poll_landuse_metrics_median %>%
    select(-landscape_level_1, -landscape_level_2) %>%
    column_to_rownames("location") %>%
    scale(), 
  method = "pearson"
  )
```

Plot correlation matrix.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
corrplot(
  poll_landuse_metrics_correlation,
  method = "number",
  order = "hclust",
  addrect = 5
  )
```

```{r}
library(corrplot)

# Correlation matrix (as you already have)
poll_landuse_metrics_correlation <- cor(
  poll_landuse_metrics_median %>%
    dplyr::select(-landscape_level_1, -landscape_level_2) %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("location") %>%
    scale(),
  method = "pearson"
)

# A diverging palette centred at 0 (easy to interpret)
col_pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#B2182B", "white", "#2166AC"))(200)

svglite("landscapemetrics_correlation.svg",
         width = 12, height = 8)

corrplot(
  poll_landuse_metrics_correlation,
  method = "color",
  type = "upper",
  order = "hclust",
  addrect = 3,
  tl.col = "black",
  tl.srt = 45,
  diag = FALSE,
  col = colorRampPalette(c("#B2182B", "white", "#2166AC"))(200),
  addCoef.col = "black",
  number.cex = 0.7,
  cl.cex = 0.9,
  mar = c(0,0,1,0)
)

dev.off()
```


There appear to be 4 groups of highly correlated variables:

Group 1:

- Mean and Standard Deviation of of Patch Area (*area_mn* and *area_sd*), Mean Contiguity (*mean_contig*), Patch Cohesion (*cohesion*), Contagion (*contag*), and Largest Patch Index (*lpi*) are all strongly positively correlated. This group is strongly negatively correlated to groups 3 and 5.

Group 2: 

- Standard Deviation and Coefficient of Variation (*contig_cv* and *contig_sv*) are strongly positively correlated to each other, and strongly negatively correlated to the mean Contiguity.

Group 3:

- Diversity indexes, entropy (*ent* and *joinent*), and interspertion and juxtaposition index (*iji*) all relate to **landscape class diversity**, and are all strongly positively correlated. 
**Kept Shannon Diversity Index (SHDI)**.

**LANDSCAPE FRAGMENTATION AND CONFIGURATION**

Edge Density (*ed*), Total Edge (*te*), Number of Patches (*np*), Patch Density (*pd*), and Conditional Entropy (*condent*) are all strongly positively correlated. They tend to increase with fragmentation.

Mean and Standard Deviation of patch area is strongly and negatively correlated to the above metrics. They tend to decrease with fragmentation.

Kept Number of Patches (*np*).

## Principal Components Analysis

Run PCA.

```{r}
poll_landuse_metrics_pca <- PCA(
 poll_landuse_metrics_median %>%
    column_to_rownames("location"),
  scale.unit = TRUE,
  quali.sup = 24:25,
  graph = FALSE
  )
```

Check variance.

```{r}
poll_landuse_metrics_pca$eig %>% datatable()

fviz_screeplot(poll_landuse_metrics_pca, ncp=10)
```

**The first 4 dimensions together explain almost 90% of variation**.

Check variable contribution to each of the three dimensions.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

poll_landuse_metrics_pca$var$cos2 %>% datatable()
poll_landuse_metrics_pca$var$cos2 %>% heatmap()

fviz_pca_var(axes = c(1,2),
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  col.var = "cos2",
  gradient.cols = c("black", "orange", "green"),
  repel = TRUE
  )

fviz_pca_var(axes = c(1,3),
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  col.var = "cos2",
  gradient.cols = c("black", "orange", "green"),
  repel = TRUE
  )

fviz_pca_var(axes = c(2,3),
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  col.var = "cos2",
  gradient.cols = c("black", "orange", "green"),
  repel = TRUE
  )
```

Dim1:
- Most influenced by **cohesion, area_sd, lpi, contag, area_mn**, metrics which are highly correlated and whose values tend to decrease with landscape fragmentation;
- Most influenced by **joinent, pd, np, sidi, shdi, ent**, metrics whose values tend to increase with fragmentation.
- Related to landscape fragmentation; 

Dim2:
- Most influenced by **area_cv, te, ed, condent**, metrics which are highly correlated and whose values tend to increase with landscape fragmentation and complexity;
- Most influenced by **ent, shdi, prd, pr, sidi, siei**, metrics which are higly correlated and whose values tend to increase with landscape fragmentation and complexity.

Dim3: 
- Most influenced by **contig_mn, contig_cv and contig_sd**;

Check samples.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8

fviz_pca_biplot(
  axes = c(1,2),
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  label = "all",
  col.var = "black",
  habillage = 24
  )

fviz_pca_biplot(
  axes = c(1,2),
```

# teste Biplot locations + landscape metrics
```{r}
# ---------- Packages ----------
# install.packages(c("patchwork","cowplot","scales","svglite"))  # run once if needed
library(patchwork)
library(factoextra)
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)     # unit()
library(cowplot)  # get_legend()
library(scales)   # pretty_breaks(), number_format()
library(svglite)

# ---------- Themes ----------
clean_theme <- theme_void() +
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
    plot.background = element_blank(),
    legend.background = element_blank()
  )

small_panel_theme <- theme(
  plot.title = element_blank(),         # remove titles in bottom panels
  axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
  axis.text  = element_blank(),         # remove tick labels
  axis.ticks = element_blank(),         # remove ticks
  plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
)

# ---------- TOP: Individuals ----------
# One merged legend: SSF (orange triangle) and LoA (green circle)
p_ind <- fviz_pca_ind(
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  axes = c(1, 2),
  habillage = 24,
  addEllipses = TRUE,
  ellipse.level = 0.95,
  repel = TRUE,
  pointsize = 3
) +
  clean_theme +
  labs(title = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL, fill = NULL) +  # remove titles

  # Force *both* colour and shape scales to use the SAME breaks/labels
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    breaks = c("landscape_level_1_SSF", "landscape_level_1_LoA"),
    labels = c("SSF", "LoA"),
    values = c(
      "landscape_level_1_SSF" = "orange",
      "landscape_level_1_LoA" = "green3"
    )
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = NULL,
    breaks = c("landscape_level_1_SSF", "landscape_level_1_LoA"),
    labels = c("SSF", "LoA"),
    values = c(
      "landscape_level_1_SSF" = 17,  # triangle
      "landscape_level_1_LoA" = 16   # circle
    )
  ) +

  # Keep ellipse colours consistent but don't create a second legend from fill
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "landscape_level_1_SSF" = "orange",
      "landscape_level_1_LoA" = "green3"
    )
  ) +
  guides(fill = "none") +  # remove ellipse-fill legend

  # Remove the square key boxes behind symbols
  theme(
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.6, "cm")
  )


# ---------- Variables panel ----------
top_vars <- 8

# Extract percentage of variance explained
var_explained <- poll_landuse_metrics_pca$eig[, 2]

pc_lab <- function(pc) {
  paste0("PC", pc, " (", round(var_explained[pc], 1), "%)")
}

p_var12 <- fviz_pca_var(
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  axes = c(1, 2),
  col.var = "contrib",
  repel = TRUE,
  labelsize = 3,
  select.var = list(contrib = top_vars)
) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#deebf7", high = "#08306b") +
  labs(x = pc_lab(1), y = pc_lab(2)) +
  clean_theme + small_panel_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_var13 <- fviz_pca_var(
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  axes = c(1, 3),
  col.var = "contrib",
  repel = TRUE,
  labelsize = 3,
  select.var = list(contrib = top_vars)
) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#deebf7", high = "#08306b") +
  labs(x = pc_lab(1), y = pc_lab(3)) +
  clean_theme + small_panel_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_var14 <- fviz_pca_var(
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  axes = c(1, 4),
  col.var = "contrib",
  repel = TRUE,
  labelsize = 3,
  select.var = list(contrib = top_vars)
) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#deebf7", high = "#08306b") +
  labs(x = pc_lab(1), y = pc_lab(4)) +
  clean_theme + small_panel_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# ---------- Legend-only plot ----------
p_leg <- fviz_pca_var(
  poll_landuse_metrics_pca,
  axes = c(1, 2),
  col.var = "contrib",
  repel = FALSE
) +
  clean_theme +
  scale_color_gradient(
    low = "#deebf7",
    high = "#08306b",
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 8),
    labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_colourbar(
      title = "Contribution (%)",
      nbin = 150,
      ticks = TRUE,
      barheight = unit(3.8, "cm"),
      barwidth = unit(0.45, "cm")
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )

leg_only <- wrap_elements(full = cowplot::get_legend(p_leg))

# ---------- Combine final panel ----------
panel <- (p_var12 | p_var13 | p_var14 | leg_only) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 1, 0.25))

panel

# ---------- Save ----------
ggsave(
  "Figure S6.svg",

)

ggsave(

  height = 5,
  bg = "white"
)
```
